newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 8.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
--Increases to be given to 360,000 public servants who have threatened strikes will exceed the 4.5 percent threshold for the government's income policy.

--Greeks have been helping the Greek economy's recovery in more ways than one - the state gained 125 billion drachmas from national lotteries in 1996, three times the amount it received in 1990. The five private casinos meanwhile has doubled revenues since 1995.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou will kick off a three-month series of meetings on the future of the banking system when he meets with bankers and bank officials next week. The main focus is expected to be policies to be followed for state-run banks in light of international developments.

--December inflation will close at 7.5 percent, sources say, down from 7.7 percent in November. The development leaves the government optimistic about reaching targets in 1997 and creates favourable conditions for a further drop in interest rates in first half 1997.
--1997 will be the most difficult year in regards to economic issues; the requisite bold decisions must be taken, speakers at the Athens Chamber said yesterday.

--Trading at the Athens bourse continued to be buoyant for the fourth consecutive day yesterday with the speedy rise of the general price index attributed to heavy buying by foreign institutional investors. The development bodes well for the ASE's plans to draw 300 billion drachmas from the stock exchange.
--Vintners Cambas changed hands yesterday with the sale of 67 percent of its share capital to a consortium of five construction companies for 6.4 billion drachmas.

-- Inflation may have fallen to as little as 7.4 percent in December, authoritive sources say. The sources predict January inflation at 7.1 percent and the target of 6.0 percent attainable by the end of spring.

--Governor of the National Bank of Greece Theodoros Karatzas will outline the plans for the bank at today's press conference following satsifying news of profits of 46-48 billion drachmas, reduced operating costs and the bank's reorganisation of its protfolio.
--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, plans to make profits of 304 billion drachmas this year, an increase of 21.75 percent over 1996

--The civil servant's union may call off strike action planned for mid-month if the latest changes to the uniform wage scale satisfy. The decision will be known after next Monday's meeting of the executive board.

--The government is trying to redraw agricultural policy under the threat of new farmers' protests and within the boundaries set by the European Union. The new Council for Agricultural Policy will group all the interested parties when it meets for the first time on Friday.

--The government is being called upon to show its decisiveness on a number of issues still pending to turn around the lack of confidence in the private sector. Today, the development ministry is to examine the entry of state-run firms to the bourse and the National Bank is expected to announce the privatisation of all non-credit institutions owned by the Group --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
